title: Why a familiar false claim feels true
series: The decision you didn't notice making

scenes.say: You've heard it ten times. That's the problem.
A claim keeps showing up. Family group. Office chat. Your feed. By the tenth time, it just feels true.
It's called the illusory truth effect. Repeated claims are easier to process, and easy feels true.
In a 2015 study, repetition made false statements seem more believable, even when people knew the correct answer.
Repetition. Ease. A gut sense of truth. Together, they can quietly outvote what you know.
So ask yourself: do I know this, or have I just heard it a lot?
